text:
customer_acme: Hey team, we're seeing inconsistent embedding sizes across deployments for the same request. Hosted returns vectors of length 768 but our Dedicated/Private endpoints are returning 512. Same model name in the request. Help?

carlos (Support): Thanks for flagging — can you paste the exact curl you used and one example response (truncated ok)? Also which model id/version are you calling?

customer_acme: Sure. Calling model "redwood/embed-alpha:2026-02-11" via two endpoints. Curl (hosted):

```
curl -s https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood/embed-alpha:2026-02-11","input":"how to center a div"}'
```

Hosted response (truncated):
```
{"data":[{"embedding":[0.0023, -0.0009, ...], "index":0}], "meta":{"vector_size":768}}
```

And Dedicated (same request, different base url):

```
curl -s https://dedicated-us-east.redwood.internal/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $DED_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood/embed-alpha:2026-02-11","input":"how to center a div"}'
```

Dedicated response (truncated):
```
{"data":[{"embedding":[0.0011, -0.0007, ...], "index":0}], "meta":{"vector_size":512}}
```

customer_acme: We also tried a Private deployment (on-prem) and got 512 there too. This is causing our similarity matching to break. Batch size was 8 for all tests. No errors in the API response, just the shorter vector.

carlos (Support): Ack. Possible causes: different model variant (alias resolution), model metadata mismatch, or an internal routing rule sending dedicated/private to a compact quantized variant. Can you provide request headers (esp. any x-model-alias or x-deployment headers) and a request id if present?

customer_acme: Here's one hosted request id header: x-request-id: req_9742f1b2. For Dedicated: req_9742ff99. No x-model-alias in our client. We do pass header: X-Customer-Tenant: acme-corp.

emma (SRE): I pulled logs for both req ids. Hosted (req_9742f1b2) routed to host pool -> model_id: redwood/embed-alpha v2026-02-11 -> backend_variant: "embed-alpha.fp16". Dedicated (req_9742ff99) routed to dedicated-pool -> model_id: redwood/embed-alpha v2026-02-11 -> backend_variant: "embed-alpha.compact8". That explains the size difference: embed-alpha.compact8 is configured to output 512.

devon (ML Eng): Interesting — compact variants usually change quantization/precision, but dimension changes mean a different architecture or a different head. How did compact8 get mapped to the same model alias?

emma (SRE): It looks like a model mapping entry was updated in the dedicated deployment's model manifest: alias "redwood/embed-alpha" was bound to two different artifact groups. Hosted uses manifest v4, dedicated manifest had a manual override to v3-compact during the last maintenance for memory pressure (ticket infra-987). The override wasn't annotated with a rollout tag.

carlos (Support): OK steps to resolve: 1) Rebind dedicated/private pool to the correct artifact (embed-alpha.fp16) 2) Invalidate any routing caches 3) Re-run a small embedded parity test (single input) and share logs 4) Consider a deprecation note on compact variant if it changes vector size.

devon (ML Eng): Also confirm metadata endpoint for the artifact: GET /v1/models/redwood/embed-alpha/versions/2026-02-11 returns embedding_size in metadata — use that as the source of truth. Example:

```
# hosted
GET https://api.redwood.ai/v1/models/redwood/embed-alpha/versions/2026-02-11
Response: {"id":"redwood/embed-alpha","version":"2026-02-11","embedding_size":768}

# dedicated (current bad mapping)
GET https://dedicated-us-east.redwood.internal/v1/models/redwood/embed-alpha/versions/2026-02-11
Response: {"id":"redwood/embed-alpha","version":"2026-02-11","embedding_size":512}
```

carlos (Support): devon — can you confirm which deploy manifest contains the override? Emma, can you attach the manifest diff?

emma (SRE): Pasted diff from dedicated manifest (redacted):
```
- model_bindings:
-  - alias: redwood/embed-alpha
-    artifact: embed-alpha.fp16
+ model_bindings:
+  - alias: redwood/embed-alpha
+    artifact: embed-alpha.compact8
```

emma (SRE): That change landed as part of infra-987 rollback step. The engineer intended to reduce peak memory but didn't realize compact8 changes the head. I'll revert the binding to embed-alpha.fp16 and pin a canary for 5% traffic to confirm parity.

customer_acme: Thanks — what's the expected downtime or side effects of reverting the binding? Our pipeline depends on vector length staying the same.

emma (SRE): No downtime — we will update model binding in control plane, invalidate routing cache, and warm the dedicated pool. For safety: 1) update binding, 2) run parity test (single input) against dedicated/private, 3) if pass, gradually roll traffic back to normal. Should be < 15 minutes.

devon (ML Eng): After revert, also run evaluation across a canonical prompt set (100 samples) to ensure embedding distribution stats match (mean cosine similarity > 0.98 with hosted). I'll run that and post results.

carlos (Support): customer_acme — can you hold off mass ingestion for the next 30 minutes while we flip? We'll DM when safe.

deploy-bot: Started job deploy/manifest-revert/infra-987 for dedicated-us-east at 1764502330. Job id: job_559ab

emma (SRE): Revert applied, cache invalidated, warming nodes. Parity single-test:
- Hosted vector_size=768
- Dedicated vector_size=768
- Request ids: hosted=req_9742f1b2 (prev), dedicated=req_9750a1de (new)

devon (ML Eng): Ran 100-sample eval. Mean cosine(hosted,dedicated)=0.992, std=0.012. Looks good.

customer_acme: Verified on our side: vectors are 768 now and similarity matches previous baseline. Thanks everyone.

carlos (Support): Closing the escalation. Follow-ups: (1) add a manifest validation rule to block artifact bindings that change embedding_size, (2) add a rollout annotation requirement for memory/power overrides, (3) update runbook for parity checks. I'll open tickets.

emma (SRE): Filed ticket infra-1122 for manifest validation, assigning to devon for the metric threshold.

devon (ML Eng): I'll add an automated parity test that runs on binding changes (compare small eval set).

customer_acme: Appreciate the quick turnaround :thumbsup:

carlos (Support): Marking thread resolved. If you see any regressions ping us and we'll reopen.
